items.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023
items.q: “What happened to Pat Metheny?” “Oh he left and moved to New York.” “Well where is Mark Egan?” “Oh he moved to New York.” “Oh well where’s Patty Scialfa?” “Oh she moved to New York.”

ctx.x: Absolutely. So when I moved to New York it was the late 70s, okay? And there was a preparation for that. I was, during my years at the University of Miami I sang six nights a week, three sets 9:00 to 1:00 in any venue that would hire me. Most of the gigs, back then when you booked a gig it lasted for a year, or it lasted for at least, at a minimum a month and then some other artist would come in and then you’d come back in in a month, you know two months later and it was like that sort of thing. So the way I kind…

for that gig there was a meeting. The president of the hotel wanted to talk to me without the band, okay? This was kind of scary, you know you do your audition, you do your four or five songs and then the owner of the hotel wants to talk to you. So I go into his office and he was very, very, you know I guess very classy fellow he was, and he just said, “Well we were wondering, Miss Lundy, would you consider changing your name?” Because the room that I would be playing for that full year is called the Mona Lisa…
‘Twisted’ in D.” In D? And the piano player would go, “D?” You know you don’t mean F? You don’t mean B flat? You know what I mean? “You mean ‘Twisted’ in D?”
